7b03d379-0490-4687-9f43-205b42619e40.description: The Diploma in Commerce (12 months) is a UWA College pathway program delivered by INTO for international students whose first language may not be English or who do not meet UWA's standard entry requirements, and/or whose intake timing is out of phase with UWA's normal first year start date. It develops English competence, academic study skills and business subject knowledge, and on successful completion carries 48 transferable credits into the second year of UWA's Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Business.
7b03d379-0490-4687-9f43-205b42619e40.curriculum: 54 points total. Compulsory units (30 points): ACCX1101 Financial Accounting, ECOX1101 Microeconomics, Prices and Markets, ENGX1001 Academic and Communication Skills for Business, ENGX1002 Professional and Academic Communications, MKTX1203 Introduction to Marketing. Remaining 24 points come from elective groups covering statistics, finance or management options, a conditional mathematics unit depending on prior qualifications, and further electives, with available specialisation areas including Accounting, Business Law, Economics, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing and Management.
7b03d379-0490-4687-9f43-205b42619e40.admission_requirements: An ATAR of at least 65, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's ATAR of 70, reflecting the longer, more gradual 12 month structure).
7b03d379-0490-4687-9f43-205b42619e40.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 5.5, with no band less than 5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's IELTS 6.0 requirement).

65e3cbce-a8d4-4385-a29c-478531549898.description: The Diploma in Commerce (8 months) is a UWA College pathway program delivered by INTO, designed for international students whose first language may not be English or who fall short of UWA's direct entry requirements for the Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Business. It builds English language competence, academic study skills and business specific subject knowledge so students can progress directly into the second year of a UWA Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Business degree, carrying 48 transferable credits on successful completion.
65e3cbce-a8d4-4385-a29c-478531549898.curriculum: 48 points total. Core units (24 points, all mandatory): ACCX1101 Financial Accounting, ECOX1101 Microeconomics, Prices and Markets, ENGX1002 Professional and Academic Communications, MKTX1203 Introduction to Marketing. Conditional unit: STAX1520 Economic and Business Statistics (6 points). Elective choice (6 points): FINX1221 Introduction to Finance or MGMX1135 Organisational Behaviour. Mathematics requirement (6 points, if needed): MATX1720 Mathematics Fundamentals. Remaining electives (6 points) chosen from CITX1401, ECOX1102, LAWX1104, MATX1721, MGMX1136 or MKTX1204.
65e3cbce-a8d4-4385-a29c-478531549898.admission_requirements: An ATAR of at least 70, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (this is the higher, faster 8 month stream, the 12 month stream accepts a lower ATAR of 65).
65e3cbce-a8d4-4385-a29c-478531549898.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 6.0, with no band less than 5.5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA. Students who do not meet this can combine an English language (ELICOS) course through UWA CELT with the diploma.

9b5fa82f-6d53-4fe2-b08c-25fce0123062._name: Diploma in Computer and Data Science - 12 months
9b5fa82f-6d53-4fe2-b08c-25fce0123062.description: The Diploma in Computer and Data Science (12 months) is a UWA College pathway program delivered by INTO for international students whose first language may not be English, who may fall short of direct entry requirements, or whose intake timing does not match UWA's standard start date. It prepares students for entry into the second year of a UWA Bachelor of Science majoring in Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Data Science, carrying 48 transferable credits on completion.
9b5fa82f-6d53-4fe2-b08c-25fce0123062.curriculum: 54 points total. Core units (36 points, all mandatory): CITX1003 Introduction to Cybersecurity, CITX1401 Computational Thinking with Python, CITX1402 Relational Database Management Systems, ENGX1003 Academic and Communication Skills for Sciences, ENGX1004 Communicating Science, STAX1400 Statistics for Science. Remaining 18 points of electives are chosen from science, business and specialised pathway options aligned with the Computer Science, Cybersecurity and Data Science majors.
9b5fa82f-6d53-4fe2-b08c-25fce0123062.admission_requirements: An ATAR of at least 65, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's ATAR of 70).
9b5fa82f-6d53-4fe2-b08c-25fce0123062.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 5.5, with no band less than 5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's IELTS 6.0 requirement).

bb2f85a0-8d69-46a4-a61a-21bee027f473._name: Diploma in Computer and Data Science 8 Months
bb2f85a0-8d69-46a4-a61a-21bee027f473.description: The Diploma in Computer and Data Science (8 months) is a UWA College pathway program delivered by INTO, built for overseas students whose first language may not be English. It provides accelerated preparation for entry into the second year of a UWA Bachelor of Science majoring in Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Data Science, carrying 48 transferable credits on successful completion.
bb2f85a0-8d69-46a4-a61a-21bee027f473.curriculum: 48 points total. Core units (30 points, all mandatory): CITX1003 Introduction to Cybersecurity, CITX1401 Computational Thinking with Python, CITX1402 Relational Database Management Systems, ENGX1004 Communicating Science, STAX1400 Statistics for Science. Elective units (18 points) chosen from approved options including CHEX1003 Introductory Chemistry, FINX1221 Introduction to Finance, MGMX1135 Organisational Behaviour, MKTX1203 Introduction to Marketing and others.
bb2f85a0-8d69-46a4-a61a-21bee027f473.admission_requirements: An ATAR of at least 70, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (this is the higher, faster stream, the 12 month stream accepts ATAR 65).
bb2f85a0-8d69-46a4-a61a-21bee027f473.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 6.0, with no band less than 5.5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA.

91901e45-22ff-4dfc-91ce-43dc7bf6699c.description: The UWA Foundation Program (8 months, UWC00) is a UWA College non-award pathway program delivered by INTO, giving international students entry into the first year of a broad range of UWA Bachelor's degrees across Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Biomedical Science, Commerce, Engineering, Mathematics, Science and Computing. It develops English language competence, study skills, subject specific knowledge and familiarity with Australian academic practices to Year 12 equivalent standard.
91901e45-22ff-4dfc-91ce-43dc7bf6699c.curriculum: 48 points total. Core units (24 points, all mandatory): ANTX0407 Australian Society, POLX0001 Contemporary World Issues, SKLX0001 EAP Part 1, Academic Skills for Foundation Studies, SKLX0002 EAP Part 2, Critical Thinking and Communication, plus non-credit AACE1000 Academic Conduct Essentials and INDG1000 Indigenous Studies Essentials. Mathematics (minimum 1 unit, 6 points): MATX0720 Mathematics Fundamentals, MATX0721 Mathematics Foundations, Methods, or MATX0722 Mathematics Foundations, Specialist. Commerce/Business (minimum 1 unit, 6 points): ACCX0101, ECOX0101, INMX0103 or MGMX0136. Science/Technology (minimum 1 unit, 6 points): BIOX0001, CHEX0003, CITX0001 or PHYX0030. Remaining elective (to reach 48 points): COMX0001 Media and Communication.
91901e45-22ff-4dfc-91ce-43dc7bf6699c.admission_requirements: A WAM (weighted average mark) of at least 70 in Australian Year 11 subjects, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (higher than the 12 month Extended stream's WAM of 65, reflecting the shorter, faster structure).
91901e45-22ff-4dfc-91ce-43dc7bf6699c.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 6.0, with no band less than 5.5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (higher than the 12 month Extended stream's IELTS 5.5 requirement).

1ce182ae-d221-476b-8c5d-9d31e773c12e.description: The UWA Foundation Program Extended (12 months, UWC10) is a UWA College non-award pathway program delivered by INTO, giving international students entry into the first year of a broad range of UWA Bachelor's degrees across Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Biomedical Science, Commerce, Engineering, Mathematics, Science and Computing. It runs longer than the standard 8 month Foundation stream to build English language competence and subject knowledge for students who need more preparation time. Students in the February intake may also be eligible for Assured Pathways to Medicine or Dentistry.
1ce182ae-d221-476b-8c5d-9d31e773c12e.curriculum: 72 points total. Core units (36 points, all mandatory): ANTX0407 Australian Society, ENGX0003 Advanced Integrated Language Skills, MATX0720 Mathematics Fundamentals, POLX0001 Contemporary World Issues, SKLX0001 EAP Part 1, Academic Skills for Foundation Studies, SKLX0002 EAP Part 2, Critical Thinking and Communication, plus non-credit AACE1000 Academic Conduct Essentials and INDG1000 Indigenous Studies Essentials. Science/Technology (minimum 1 unit, 6 points): BIOX0001 Foundation Biology, CHEX0003 Foundation Chemistry, CITX0001 Foundation Computing or PHYX0030 Foundation Physics. Remaining points (to reach 72) chosen from ACCX0101 Introduction to Business and Accounting, COMX0001 Media and Communication, ECOX0101 Introduction to Economics, INMX0103 Information, Technology and Systems, MATX0721 Mathematics Foundations, Methods, MATX0722 Mathematics Foundations, Specialist and MGMX0136 Management and Organisations.
1ce182ae-d221-476b-8c5d-9d31e773c12e.admission_requirements: A WAM (weighted average mark) of at least 65 in Australian Year 11 subjects, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's WAM of 70).
1ce182ae-d221-476b-8c5d-9d31e773c12e.english_requirements: An IELTS score of at least 5.5, with no band less than 5, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (lower than the 8 month stream's IELTS 6.0 requirement).

a29c52fb-672f-425c-a477-a911cce627bd.description: This is a Doctor of Philosophy undertaken in the field of human and behavioural sciences at the University of Western Australia. Like all UWA PhDs, it is a higher degree by research completed entirely through independent research and the preparation of a thesis under academic supervision, rather than through coursework. Candidates work with supervisors in schools such as Psychological Science to design and carry out an original research project examining aspects of human behaviour, cognition, or social and psychological processes, developing advanced skills in research design, critical analysis, methodology and scholarly communication at the highest academic level. The degree suits students aiming for careers in academic research, applied behavioural science, or research intensive professional roles.
a29c52fb-672f-425c-a477-a911cce627bd.curriculum: The degree has no formal coursework units and is instead structured entirely around a supervised, independent research project and thesis. Standard full time candidature is 4 years (a maximum of 24 credit points equivalent per semester), with a maximum completion time limit of 8 years. Candidates may submit a thesis as a monograph, a series of papers (typically up to three first authored papers, to a maximum of five), a hybrid of chapters and papers, or, where relevant, creative work accompanied by a scholarly exegesis of at least 20,000 words. Theses generally run to approximately 80,000 to 100,000 words and are examined by written report followed by an oral defence (viva voce) before academic examiners.
a29c52fb-672f-425c-a477-a911cce627bd.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from UWA, or a qualification recognised by the Board of the Graduate Research School as equivalent, and must demonstrate adequate research preparation in line with UWA's Adequate Research Preparation Policy, typically an Honours degree at upper second class level or higher (or a research masters, or equivalent research training and experience) in a relevant discipline such as psychology or a related behavioural science. Applicants must also identify and secure agreement from an eligible UWA academic supervisor before applying.
a29c52fb-672f-425c-a477-a911cce627bd.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

10fae6ff-8551-4229-a1f7-8c56e4f67318.description: This is a Doctor of Philosophy undertaken in the field of human and social geography at the University of Western Australia, based in the Geography and Planning discipline area. As with all UWA PhDs, it is a higher degree by research undertaken entirely through independent research and the preparation of a thesis, rather than coursework. Candidates work with academic supervisors to design and carry out original research into human and social dimensions of geography, such as population change, urban and regional development, environmental policy and planning, or applied human geography, developing advanced research design, analytical and scholarly writing skills at the highest academic level.
10fae6ff-8551-4229-a1f7-8c56e4f67318.curriculum: The degree has no formal coursework units and centres on a supervised, independent research project and thesis. Standard full time candidature is 4 years (24 credit points equivalent per semester), with a maximum completion time limit of 8 years. Theses may be submitted as a monograph, a series of papers (typically up to three first authored papers, to a maximum of five), a hybrid of chapters and papers, or creative work with an accompanying scholarly exegesis of at least 20,000 words. Theses generally run to approximately 80,000 to 100,000 words and are examined by written report followed by an oral defence (viva voce).
10fae6ff-8551-4229-a1f7-8c56e4f67318.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from UWA, or a qualification recognised by the Board of the Graduate Research School as equivalent, and must demonstrate adequate research preparation under UWA's Adequate Research Preparation Policy, typically an Honours degree at upper second class level or higher (or a research masters, or equivalent research training and experience) in geography or a related discipline. Applicants must identify and secure agreement from an eligible UWA academic supervisor, normally within the discipline of Geography and Planning, before applying.
10fae6ff-8551-4229-a1f7-8c56e4f67318.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

b45e0015-ea24-4047-8932-b57d59594d95._name: Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Neuropsychology
b45e0015-ea24-4047-8932-b57d59594d95.description: This is a combined four year professional and research doctoral pathway (course code 01890/54590) that packages the Master of Clinical Neuropsychology with a PhD. It is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) and is designed to produce clinical neuropsychologists grounded in the scientist practitioner tradition, who combine high level clinical competence with the ability to advance the discipline through original research. Graduates who complete the program become eligible to apply for general registration with the Psychology Board of Australia and may pursue endorsement in clinical neuropsychology after completing the Board's Registrar Program. This combined pathway is not being offered for new entry in 2026, though it remains an active accredited program in UWA's handbook.
b45e0015-ea24-4047-8932-b57d59594d95.curriculum: The course totals 264 credit points over a standard 4 year full time candidature (8 year maximum). It combines 72 points of mandatory coursework, including Applied Research Methods, Assessment and Intervention (Adult Complex Disorders), Child and Adolescent Clinical Psychology and Neuropsychology, Human Neuroanatomy and Neuropsychology, Foundations in Clinical Skills I and II, and Assessment and Intervention (Emotional Disorders), with supervised clinical placements totalling at least 730 hours across two placement blocks. The research component is a PhD thesis of a minimum of 24 points undertaken in the area of clinical neuropsychology, governed by the standard Doctor of Philosophy rules, with a research proposal required within 6 months of enrolment.
b45e0015-ea24-4047-8932-b57d59594d95.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold an APAC accredited Honours degree (or equivalent) in psychology with a mark of at least upper second class Honours (2A) completed within the last 10 years, or hold current registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia (Ahpra). Applicants must be eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with the Board, and must secure agreement from at least one PhD supervisor who is an academic staff member of the School of Psychological Science before applying. Selection is competitive and considers a personal statement, two referee reports, a curriculum vitae, and an interview, subject to an annual intake quota.
b45e0015-ea24-4047-8932-b57d59594d95.english_requirements: Higher tier, the tier UWA applies to this combined professional and clinical registration pathway (matching the equivalent Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Psychology admission standard, whose own handbook page states this table directly): IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no band below 6.5, PTE Academic overall 66 with no communicative skill below 56, TOEFL iBT overall 94 (Listening/Reading 24, Speaking 23, Writing 24). Applicants must also separately meet the Psychology Board of Australia's current Registration Standard for English Language Skills.

4526fc32-8e5c-49fe-97fe-e07d49d25926._name: Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Psychology
4526fc32-8e5c-49fe-97fe-e07d49d25926.description: This is a combined four year professional and research doctoral pathway (course code 01870/54570) that synthesises the Master of Clinical Psychology with a PhD. It follows a scientist practitioner model intended for students aiming to become future leaders in clinical psychology by combining high level clinical practice skills with the capacity to advance the discipline through original research. The program is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC); graduates become eligible for general registration with the Psychology Board of Australia and may pursue endorsement in clinical psychology after completing the Board's Registrar Program. This combined pathway is not being offered for new entry in 2026, though it remains an active accredited program in UWA's handbook.
4526fc32-8e5c-49fe-97fe-e07d49d25926.curriculum: The course runs over a standard 4 year full time candidature (8 year maximum) and includes 72 credit points of mandatory coursework: Foundations in Clinical Skills I and II, Assessment and Intervention units covering Childhood, Emotional, and Adult Complex Disorders, Applied Research Methods, and Special Topics in Clinical Psychology. Coursework is paired with two supervised clinical placements totalling a minimum of 400 face to face clinical hours, plus associated supervision and workshops. The research component is a PhD thesis undertaken in a clinical psychology specialisation area, governed by the standard Doctor of Philosophy rules, with formal supervisory approval of the research topic required within 6 months of enrolment.
4526fc32-8e5c-49fe-97fe-e07d49d25926.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold an APAC accredited Honours degree in psychology with a mark of at least upper second class Honours (2A), completed within the last 10 years, or hold current registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia (Ahpra). Applicants must be eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with the Board and must secure agreement from at least one PhD supervisor who is an academic staff member of the School of Psychological Science before applying, including a supervisory agreement and research project outline submitted with the application. Selection considers a personal statement, two referee reports, a curriculum vitae, and an interview.
4526fc32-8e5c-49fe-97fe-e07d49d25926.english_requirements: Higher tier: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no band below 6.5 (Writing may be 6.5), PTE Academic overall 66 with Writing not below 56 and other skills not below 66, TOEFL iBT overall 94 (Listening/Reading 24, Speaking 23, Writing 24). Applicants must also separately meet the Psychology Board of Australia's current Registration Standard for English Language Skills.

fb035705-a4d0-468b-a856-043d90967169._name: Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Industrial and Organisational Psychology
fb035705-a4d0-468b-a856-043d90967169.description: This is a combined four year professional and research doctoral pathway (course code 01880/54580) that packages the Master of Industrial and Organisational Psychology with a PhD. Industrial and organisational psychology applies psychological knowledge and methods to workplaces, aiming to improve organisational effectiveness and the quality of working life. The program is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) and leads toward professional registration, with graduates eligible to use the specialist title of Organisational Psychologist after registration requirements are met. This combined pathway is not being offered for new entry in 2026, though it remains an active accredited program in UWA's handbook.
fb035705-a4d0-468b-a856-043d90967169.curriculum: The combined course totals 264 credit points over a standard 4 year full time candidature (8 year maximum). The Master's component contributes 72 points of coursework across nine units, including Research Methods in Applied Settings, Assessment and Selection, Organisational Development and Change, MIOP Professional Practice and Ethics, Psychology of Leadership and Coaching, Psychology of Training, and Health, Safety and Human Factors at Work, together with three supervised practical placements of 45 days each (1,000 hours total) across three different organisational settings. The research component is a PhD thesis undertaken in the area of industrial and organisational psychology, governed by the standard Doctor of Philosophy rules, with a research proposal required within 6 months of enrolment.
fb035705-a4d0-468b-a856-043d90967169.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold an APAC accredited Honours degree in psychology with a mark of at least upper second class Honours (2A), completed within the last 10 years, or hold current registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia (Ahpra). Applicants must be eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with the Board and must secure agreement from at least one PhD supervisor who is an academic staff member of the School of Psychological Science before applying. Selection is competitive, considering a personal statement, two referee reports, a curriculum vitae demonstrating relevant experience, and (for eligible candidates) an interview, subject to an annual intake quota.
fb035705-a4d0-468b-a856-043d90967169.english_requirements: Higher tier, matching the equivalent combined clinical psychology and clinical neuropsychology doctoral pathways whose own handbook page states this table directly: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no band below 6.5, PTE Academic overall 66 with no communicative skill below 56, TOEFL iBT overall 94 (Listening/Reading 24, Speaking 23, Writing 24). Applicants must also separately meet the Psychology Board of Australia's current Registration Standard for English Language Skills.

1cbdcda0-ee9a-4fa8-b975-bab1ba400acb._name: Master of Philosophy (Agricultural Economics, Plant and Soil Sciences)
1cbdcda0-ee9a-4fa8-b975-bab1ba400acb.description: This is a Master of Philosophy undertaken across the combined discipline area of agricultural economics and plant and soil sciences at the University of Western Australia (the DB's stored name is truncated, the full discipline pairing, confirmed independently via the Good Universities Guide and Uni Enrol, is Agricultural Economics, Plant and Soil Sciences). Like UWA's other Master of Philosophy programs, it is a two year higher degree by research undertaken entirely through independent research, allowing candidates to investigate an original research question spanning agricultural economics (such as farm business decision making, agribusiness or resource economics) together with plant or soil science, under supervision from the relevant UWA school, typically the UWA School of Agriculture and Environment.
1cbdcda0-ee9a-4fa8-b975-bab1ba400acb.curriculum: The program has no formal coursework component and is centred entirely on a supervised research project and thesis, culminating in a viva voce (oral) examination. Standard full time candidature is 2 years, with progress milestones typically including a research proposal at around 6 months, an annual progress review at 12 months, thesis submission at around 21 months, and examination and completion by 24 months. Theses may take the form of a monograph, a series of papers, a hybrid format, or creative work with a scholarly exegesis, and are limited to approximately 40,000 to 50,000 words including footnotes.
1cbdcda0-ee9a-4fa8-b975-bab1ba400acb.admission_requirements: Applicants must demonstrate adequate research preparation under UWA's Adequate Research Preparation Policy, generally an Honours degree (or equivalent) in agricultural economics, agribusiness, plant science, soil science or a closely related agricultural discipline, and must satisfy the University's English language competence requirement and the other conditions of the HDR Admission Policy. As with other UWA research degrees, applicants must identify and secure agreement from an eligible academic supervisor in the relevant school before applying.
1cbdcda0-ee9a-4fa8-b975-bab1ba400acb.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

0dda02ff-546e-419d-8642-c3ed321782b0.description: This is UWA's Master of Philosophy research degree undertaken in the field of public health, distinct from the coursework based Master of Public Health. It is a two year higher degree by research based in the School of Population and Global Health, allowing candidates who have already built a foundation in public health (commonly through a Master of Public Health with a substantial dissertation component) to pursue an original, supervised research project examining a public health question, such as epidemiology, health policy, biostatistics or population health topics, culminating in a thesis.
0dda02ff-546e-419d-8642-c3ed321782b0.curriculum: The program has no formal coursework component and is structured entirely around a supervised research project and thesis, examined by written report and a viva voce (oral) examination. Standard full time candidature is 2 years, with typical milestones of a research proposal at around 6 months, an annual progress review at 12 months, thesis submission at around 21 months, and examination and completion by 24 months. Theses may be submitted as a monograph, a series of papers, a hybrid format, or creative work with a scholarly exegesis, and are limited to approximately 40,000 to 50,000 words including footnotes.
0dda02ff-546e-419d-8642-c3ed321782b0.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a relevant degree, generally an Honours degree (or equivalent research preparation, such as a Master of Public Health with a substantial dissertation component) in public health, medicine, epidemiology or a closely related discipline, satisfying UWA's Adequate Research Preparation Policy. Applicants must identify and secure agreement from an eligible academic supervisor in the School of Population and Global Health before applying.
0dda02ff-546e-419d-8642-c3ed321782b0.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18 (a program specific listing corroborates the same PTE figure).

86fe5056-c7ac-4f6e-93e7-0716f81c0e99.curriculum: The degree is a thesis only research masters administered by the Graduate Research School. Students complete a course of supervised independent research and must submit a thesis of no more than 30,000 words on an aspect of social work theory, practice or policy, examined by external examiners. The standard full time duration is 1 year (48 points), with a maximum time limit of 4 years.
86fe5056-c7ac-4f6e-93e7-0716f81c0e99.admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed the requirements for the Graduate Diploma in Advanced Social Work at UWA, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Faculty, and have at least two years' experience as a professionally qualified social worker.
86fe5056-c7ac-4f6e-93e7-0716f81c0e99.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

8a22d95b-2a39-4741-8569-d379a2bc4ebf.description: The Master of Architecture (Design) is a program of independent, supervised research leading to the presentation of an exhibition of architectural design equivalent in scope to the schematic design of a building of major cultural significance. It is a research masters by creative work (course code 25760), distinct from UWA's coursework Master of Architecture, administered by the Graduate Research School over a standard 2 year, 96 point enrolment.
8a22d95b-2a39-4741-8569-d379a2bc4ebf.curriculum: Over a standard 2 year, 96 point enrolment, students undertake independent supervised research leading to an exhibition of architectural design equivalent in scope to the schematic design of a building of major cultural significance. Within four months of first enrolment, students submit a research proposal covering the brief, scope of works and estimated construction costs. For examination, students present the exhibition together with an A3 volume containing the exhibition drawings, photographs of the models, the approved research proposal, and an expanded abstract of up to 5,000 words explaining how the design proposal contributes to the discipline of architecture. The exhibition is examined by a committee including the Dean of the Faculty of Architecture, Landscape and Visual Arts and external examiners, and students may later apply to upgrade candidature to the Doctor of Architecture (Design).
8a22d95b-2a39-4741-8569-d379a2bc4ebf.admission_requirements: In addition to the Graduate Research School's general admission rules, applicants must have sufficient architectural design experience, as determined by the Graduate Research School Board on the recommendation of the Head of the School of Architecture, Landscape and Visual Arts.
8a22d95b-2a39-4741-8569-d379a2bc4ebf.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

0705c4f4-f5e2-42d6-b0e7-b7dc71797a2a._name: Master of Curatorial Studies in Fine Arts (research)
0705c4f4-f5e2-42d6-b0e7-b7dc71797a2a.curriculum: Over a standard 2 year, 96 point enrolment, students complete a placement of at least one day a week for 36 weeks in a public gallery or comparable institution (MCur Placement), plus a comparative report of up to 5,000 words on that placement, and a component of Advanced Curatorial Studies. For the main research component, students present one of: an Exhibition Proposal of at least 5,000 words together with an Exhibition Catalogue essay of at least 25,000 words; an MCur Dissertation of at least 30,000 words on an aspect of museology relevant to curatorial practice; or a catalogue raisonne of up to 30,000 words on the works of an uncatalogued artist.
0705c4f4-f5e2-42d6-b0e7-b7dc71797a2a.admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed a bachelor's degree of at least four years' full time study (or the part time equivalent) in a subject area the Dean of the Faculty of Architecture, Landscape and Visual Arts considers relevant to curatorial studies, or an equivalent qualification, and satisfy the Graduate Research School Board that they have the general ability to complete the course and the special ability to prepare and present a thesis.
0705c4f4-f5e2-42d6-b0e7-b7dc71797a2a.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

28922ee8-a7c1-4f69-bd50-46c53360c381.curriculum: Over a standard 2 year, 96 point enrolment, students present for examination an exhibition of original artwork showing technical accomplishment and imaginative resource, together with a thesis of up to 25,000 words on an aspect of arts theory, history or criticism. Full time students submit the proposed thesis topic and exhibition form for Board approval within four months of first enrolment, and must present an accompanying exegesis of up to 5,000 words. The exhibition is examined by a committee comprising the Dean of the Faculty of Architecture, Landscape and Visual Arts (or nominee) and two examiners external to UWA.
28922ee8-a7c1-4f69-bd50-46c53360c381.admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed the requirements for a bachelor's degree in an appropriate subject area from UWA, or equivalent, and have completed a qualification in Art Practice from a recognised tertiary institution, or be judged by the Graduate Research School Board to have equivalent practical expertise and professional standing. Applicants without sufficient theoretical and practical grounding in fine arts may be required to complete preliminary work.
28922ee8-a7c1-4f69-bd50-46c53360c381.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

c256b904-6d33-4b6d-b21e-600cc22462ea.curriculum: This is a 1 year, 48 point research masters offered in three fields: composition, musicology and performance. Composition students present a portfolio of composition(s) plus an 8,000 to 10,000 word thesis; musicology students present a 20,000 to 25,000 word thesis; performance students present a recital program of normally 60 to 80 minutes plus an 8,000 to 10,000 word thesis. All candidates must also demonstrate satisfactory attendance at and participation in the Conservatorium of Music's Research Seminar. The minimum enrolment period is 8 months full time (16 months part time). Students may apply to upgrade candidature to the Doctor of Musical Arts.
c256b904-6d33-4b6d-b21e-600cc22462ea.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a Bachelor of Music with honours or a Bachelor of Arts with honours from UWA, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Graduate Research School Board. Composition and musicology applicants must pass a portfolio review and interview; performance applicants must pass an audition and interview, arranged by the Head of the Conservatorium of Music.
c256b904-6d33-4b6d-b21e-600cc22462ea.english_requirements: Minimum tier, the standard requirement for all UWA Higher Degrees by Research: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, or TOEFL iBT overall 82 with a minimum of Writing 22, Speaking 20, Listening 20, Reading 18.

3eae63fe-6dd0-4c15-85db-03c7e9a6929e.curriculum: This is a coursework masters accredited by the Australian Institute of Landscape Architects, requiring 144 points overall (96 points of taught units plus up to 48 points of admission or conversion credit), with a standard 2 year full time duration extending to a maximum of 3 years. All students complete 66 points of core units, including Research Strategies in Landscape Architecture, Urban Design and Architecture; Australian Landscapes; Landscape and Urban Ecology; Critical Theory in Landscape Architecture; Landscape Professional Documents; two Design Research Studios (Making and Complexity); Landscape Professional Practice; and Landscape Dynamics. Students without a landscape architecture major must also complete conversion units of up to 48 points. Depending on pathway, students then take 30 points of option units, a Focus Area (Building Information Modelling, Environmental Planning, Social Impact Design or Urban Design) plus options, or a coursework and dissertation track.
3eae63fe-6dd0-4c15-85db-03c7e9a6929e.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, with the equivalent of a UWA weighted average mark of at least 60 per cent. Applicants who have not completed a bachelor's degree with a major in Landscape Architecture, or equivalent, must complete conversion units of up to 48 points as part of the course. After graduating, students must also complete two years of full time (or part time equivalent) supervised work experience as a Landscape Architect before applying for Registration via the Australian Institute of Landscape Architects' Mentorship Pathway.
3eae63fe-6dd0-4c15-85db-03c7e9a6929e.english_requirements: UWA's Minimum standard English Language Competence requirement applies to this course, as it does not appear on UWA's Higher standard ELC list: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no band below 60 (equivalent scores apply for other UWA accepted English tests).

40a860fd-74cf-425a-9e79-b63b79577b7f.curriculum: This is a coursework masters of up to 96 points, with a standard full time duration of 1.5 years extending to a 2 year maximum. Students first complete 24 points (4 units) of interdisciplinary breadth chosen with a course adviser across all faculties, then nominate an area of disciplinary or cross disciplinary depth and complete a minimum of 24 points (4 units) in that area, including a substantial research based project, capstone experience or piece of scholarship. Remaining units are selected as electives to support the depth area, with at least half of all units at Level 4 or 5. Students who have completed a relevant bachelor's degree major are granted credit for conversion units of up to 24 points.
40a860fd-74cf-425a-9e79-b63b79577b7f.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA. The Graduate Certificate in Studies (24 points) and Master of Studies (96 points) form an articulated sequence, so a student who withdraws from the Master of Studies after completing the Graduate Certificate requirements may apply for that lesser award instead.
40a860fd-74cf-425a-9e79-b63b79577b7f.english_requirements: UWA's Minimum standard English Language Competence requirement applies to this course, as it does not appear on UWA's Higher standard ELC list: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no band below 60 (equivalent scores apply for other UWA accepted English tests).

9fe69f63-9e90-4823-9a06-c72cb0cb0eec.curriculum: This is a 0.5 year, 24 point graduate certificate. In consultation with a course adviser, students select four postgraduate units (24 points) of interdisciplinary breadth from electives available across all UWA faculties, chosen to suit their academic, professional or personal goals. On completion, students may choose to articulate into the 96 point Master of Studies, carrying their completed units forward as part of that degree's 24 point breadth component.
9fe69f63-9e90-4823-9a06-c72cb0cb0eec.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA.
9fe69f63-9e90-4823-9a06-c72cb0cb0eec.english_requirements: UWA's Minimum standard English Language Competence requirement applies to this course, as it does not appear on UWA's Higher standard ELC list: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no band below 60 (equivalent scores apply for other UWA accepted English tests).

fbaaecd6-07d3-4012-b8fd-aa029ab73f06.description: The Doctor of Podiatry is an advanced postgraduate qualification for already qualified podiatrists who want to broaden their knowledge of podiatric medicine and surgery. The course is delivered in two stages, two semesters of coursework and practicum units covering biostatistics, research methodology and the foundations of podiatric surgery, followed by four semesters of independent doctoral level clinical research on a topic of interest. Students carry out patient oriented research, work through the ethics and communication of research, and produce an original thesis for publication. It is the highest postgraduate qualification UWA offers in podiatry and suits podiatrists wanting to combine advanced clinical practice with a research career.
fbaaecd6-07d3-4012-b8fd-aa029ab73f06.curriculum: The course totals 144 points across two components. Group A is 48 points of core coursework and practicum units, including Foundations of Podiatric Surgery 1 and 2 (PODI5511, PODI5512), Concepts of Podiatric Surgery (PODI5513), Podiatric Medicine Practicum, Introduction to Surgical Skills (PODI5515), plus supporting research methods units in biostatistics and epidemiology (PUBH4401, PUBH4403, PUBH5805). Group B is a 96 point research thesis (PODI6900 full time or PODI6902 part time), undertaken once the coursework requirements are complete. Standard full time duration is 3 years, with a 7 year maximum time limit. Students who complete only the 48 point coursework component may exit with a Graduate Diploma in Podiatric Medicine.
fbaaecd6-07d3-4012-b8fd-aa029ab73f06.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a Doctor of Podiatric Medicine from UWA, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Faculty, plus at least one year of relevant professional experience as a podiatrist. A Research and Coursework Supplementary Form must also be completed as part of the application.
fbaaecd6-07d3-4012-b8fd-aa029ab73f06.english_requirements: Applicants must meet UWA's Minimum English language competence standard: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60, as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework.

e7bc5064-1fe8-4d4f-91a4-2336c8c91ea6.description: The Doctor of Social Work is a research based and research driven advanced qualification for qualified social workers who are committed to continuing their professional education at the highest level. Candidates work closely with expert researchers on a project of their own choosing, building high calibre research skills and producing a substantial piece of original scholarship in the field of social work. The award gives graduates the top professional research qualification available in the discipline and can also be a pathway into further doctoral study such as a PhD.
e7bc5064-1fe8-4d4f-91a4-2336c8c91ea6.curriculum: The degree totals 144 points made up of two components. The coursework component is 48 points across eight mandatory units covering Advanced Research Methods, Advanced Studies, Advanced Theory and Practice, and Research Paradigms, each offered in two parts. The thesis component is 96 points, taken as either a full time or part time Doctor of Social Work Thesis, available for enrolment each semester once the coursework units are complete. Standard duration is 3 years full time, with a 6 year maximum time limit.
e7bc5064-1fe8-4d4f-91a4-2336c8c91ea6.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold one of: a Bachelor of Social Work with first or upper second class honours; a Master of Social Work (coursework and dissertation) with a Distinction or High Distinction average; a Graduate Diploma in Advanced Social Work with a weighted average mark of at least 70 per cent; a Master of Advanced Social Work; or a Master of Arts (Social Work). In addition, applicants need at least two years of full time post qualification professional experience as a social worker.
e7bc5064-1fe8-4d4f-91a4-2336c8c91ea6.english_requirements: Applicants must meet UWA's English language competence requirement as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, with a minimum overall IELTS Academic score of 6.5 with no individual band below 6.0.

f3ce8bd3-79ba-406a-aad6-aff9eb275873.description: The Graduate Certificate in Infectious Diseases introduces students to core concepts across infectious agents, disease, immunology, epidemiology and disease control, with practical training in laboratory techniques and data analysis. It is designed both as an upskilling option for professionals already working in infectious disease related fields and as an entry pathway into higher UWA qualifications in the area, namely the Graduate Diploma in Infectious Diseases and the Master of Infectious Diseases. This is a genuine standalone course with its own handbook code and curriculum, distinct from the Graduate Diploma in Infectious Diseases, though it is not being offered for new entry in 2026.
f3ce8bd3-79ba-406a-aad6-aff9eb275873.curriculum: The certificate requires 24 points. Group A contributes 18 points from units such as Foundations of Infectious Diseases, Molecular and Cellular Microbiology and Diagnostic Medical Microbiology. Group B contributes 6 points chosen from options including Biostatistics I, Epidemiology I or Clinical Laboratory Skills.
f3ce8bd3-79ba-406a-aad6-aff9eb275873.admission_requirements: Applicants need a relevant bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, together with either a UWA weighted average mark of at least 60 per cent in Level 3 units, at least three years of relevant full time professional experience, or evidence of adequate research outputs.
f3ce8bd3-79ba-406a-aad6-aff9eb275873.english_requirements: Applicants must satisfy UWA's English language competence requirement as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, corresponding to the Minimum standard of IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60.

37bd5077-5270-47af-901e-2a4380e59df5._name: Graduate Diploma in Ocean Technology and Engineering
37bd5077-5270-47af-901e-2a4380e59df5.description: The Graduate Diploma in Ocean Technology and Engineering gives students disciplinary knowledge and practical skills in oceanography, hydrodynamics and ocean engineering, preparing them for careers addressing the engineering challenges of marine renewable energy and coastal infrastructure in dynamic ocean environments. The course suits engineers and scientists wanting a focused, one year qualification bridging oceanography and applied ocean engineering practice.
37bd5077-5270-47af-901e-2a4380e59df5.curriculum: The diploma requires 48 points across eight mandatory units: Coastal and Offshore Engineering (GENG5501), Renewable Ocean Energy (OCEN4007), Ocean Observational Methods and Modelling (OCEN4010), Ocean Engineering and Technology (OCEN5002), Design of Coastal Structures (OCEN5004), Designing Offshore Structures (OCEN5005), and Offshore and Coastal Engineering Research Project Parts 1 and 2 (OCEN5411, OCEN5412). Standard duration is 1 year full time, taken as 24 points per semester, with a 2 year maximum time limit.
37bd5077-5270-47af-901e-2a4380e59df5.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a relevant bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, with a weighted average mark equivalent to at least 65 per cent.
37bd5077-5270-47af-901e-2a4380e59df5.english_requirements: Applicants must satisfy UWA's English language competence requirement as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, corresponding to the Minimum standard of IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60.

f66a6765-4d36-4376-b445-f8099baec909.description: The Master of Commerce - Articulation is a coursework only master's degree for students continuing on from a relevant UWA graduate certificate into the Master of Commerce sequence. It lets students build breadth across business disciplines including accounting, business information and logistics management, employment relations, finance, human resource management, marketing or economics. This version of the course is only available to students re-enrolling as part of an articulated pathway rather than to new direct entry applicants.
f66a6765-4d36-4376-b445-f8099baec909.curriculum: The course requires 72 points, taken as a standard full time load of 24 points per semester over 1.5 years, with a 5 year maximum time limit. Core units include Introduction to Global Business (MGMT5511) and Principles for Responsible Management (MGMT5526), with students then selecting 24 to 48 further points from designated unit groups aligned to one of nine specialisation areas: Accounting, Business Information and Logistics Management, Economics, Employment Relations, Finance, Human Resource Management, Management, and Marketing.
f66a6765-4d36-4376-b445-f8099baec909.admission_requirements: Applicants must satisfy one of: a bachelor's degree with a weighted average mark of at least 60 per cent; two or more years of professional experience in a relevant field; or completion of a relevant graduate certificate at UWA that articulates into this course.
f66a6765-4d36-4376-b445-f8099baec909.english_requirements: Applicants must satisfy UWA's English language competence requirement as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, corresponding to the Minimum standard of IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60.

734607f9-c309-4270-b2c6-2a7cb2e1057d.description: The Master of Hearing Sciences gives students comprehensive theoretical knowledge in hearing science, covering the anatomy and physiology of hearing and deafness, audiological instrumentation, assessment, rehabilitation and advanced communication devices. The course has a strong research component that can be tailored to a student's own background and interests, alongside practical training in psychoacoustics, clinical diagnosis and community audiology. Importantly, this qualification does not lead to accreditation as an audiologist in Australia, so it suits students wanting research and technical depth in hearing science rather than a clinical audiology practice pathway.
734607f9-c309-4270-b2c6-2a7cb2e1057d.curriculum: The course requires 96 points over a standard 2 year full time duration, with a 5 year maximum time limit. Students must complete 48 points of prerequisite units before advancing to higher level units, covering audiological instrumentation, adult and paediatric hearing assessment, ear diseases and hearing devices, alongside a four part research project sequence that forms the dissertation component. Delivery is internal and full time only, with intake at the beginning of the year.
734607f9-c309-4270-b2c6-2a7cb2e1057d.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, with the equivalent of a UWA weighted average mark of at least 65 per cent from their most recent degree of at least one year full time duration.
734607f9-c309-4270-b2c6-2a7cb2e1057d.english_requirements: Applicants must satisfy UWA's English language competence requirement as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, corresponding to the Minimum standard of IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall 64 with no band below 60.

6c9d6d0c-a379-4e23-a03a-992edbbe8d7d.description: The Master of Legal Practice is designed for overseas qualified lawyers who have already completed a law degree and been admitted to practice in another jurisdiction, and who have been advised by the Legal Practice Board of Western Australia to complete extra units of study before they can be admitted to practice in this state. It is the only course of its kind offered in Western Australia. Each candidate's program is tailored specifically to them, based on the requirements set by the Legal Practice Board, and successful completion gives graduates the accreditation needed to apply for admission as a solicitor or barrister in Western Australia, subject to any further requirements the Board sets.
6c9d6d0c-a379-4e23-a03a-992edbbe8d7d.curriculum: The course totals 96 points, though up to half of these points, 48, can be claimed as advanced standing from prior learning, meaning many candidates complete it in as little as one year. Students from non-common law jurisdictions must first complete a mandatory foundation unit, either Foundations of Law and Lawyering (LAWS4101) or Foundations of Law and Legal Institutions (LAWS4227). After the foundation requirement, students select 48 to 96 points from Group B essential common law units such as Criminal Law, Contract, Property Law, Torts, Land Law, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Equity and Trusts, Corporations Law, Evidence, Professional and Ethical Practice, and Procedure, plus Group C electives from more than 30 specialised units. Standard duration is 2 years, delivered internally at the Perth campus on a full time or part time basis.
6c9d6d0c-a379-4e23-a03a-992edbbe8d7d.admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a Juris Doctor or Bachelor of Laws, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, and must have an assessment from the Legal Practice Board of Western Australia setting out which units they are required to complete in order to practise in the state.
6c9d6d0c-a379-4e23-a03a-992edbbe8d7d.english_requirements: The course requires UWA's Higher English language competence standard, as set out in the University Policy on Admission, Coursework, corresponding to IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no band below 6.5, or PTE Academic overall 70 with no band below 64.

d20dd167-4f8e-4dff-bb45-a0f34986c73e.description: The Master of Teaching - Primary is a two year intensive professional teaching qualification that prepares graduates for careers as primary school teachers, with a strong clinical focus on teaching children who have difficulty with reading and mathematics alongside literacy and numeracy more broadly. Students are introduced to the full breadth of the primary curriculum, including science, music, dance, visual arts, and health and physical education, and put their teaching into practice across two extended school placements. The course is accredited by the Teacher Registration Board of Western Australia, and graduates meet the requirements for Provisional Registration with that Board. The course is not being offered in 2026, with the next intake expected in 2028.
d20dd167-4f8e-4dff-bb45-a0f34986c73e.curriculum: The course totals 96 points over a standard 2 year full time duration, with a 5 year maximum time limit. Year 1 (54 points) covers Perspectives in Aboriginal Education, Integrated Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences, Teaching Mathematics in the Early Years, Language and Literacy in the Early Years, Integrated Studies in Science, Professional Practice A (a 35 day placement), Teaching English in Middle and Upper Primary, The Artistic and Expressive Child, and Child and Adolescent Development and Pedagogy. Year 2 (42 points) covers the National Literacy and Numeracy Test, Teaching Performance Assessment, Professional Practice B (a 30 day placement), Teaching Mathematics in Middle and Upper Primary, Technologies in the Curriculum, Diverse Learners in Inclusive Classrooms, Early Reading Research and Practice, and Physical Development, Movement and Health.
d20dd167-4f8e-4dff-bb45-a0f34986c73e.admission_requirements: Applicants need a bachelor's degree, or an equivalent qualification recognised by UWA, with the equivalent of a UWA weighted average mark of at least 60 per cent, and at least one year of the bachelor's degree relevant to one or more learning areas in the primary school curriculum. Selection is competitive and applicants are ranked on personal statements and faculty interviews. International applicants must also obtain a criminal record check before admission.
d20dd167-4f8e-4dff-bb45-a0f34986c73e.english_requirements: For applicants from non-English speaking institutions, the course requires IELTS Academic overall 7.5, with a minimum of 7.0 in Reading and Writing and a minimum of 8.0 in Listening and Speaking, or PTE Academic overall 75 with no sub-score below 70, reflecting the Teacher Registration Board of Western Australia's own entry standard.

b92d45af-21a4-444b-88d3-8cd15d31b86e._name: Masters of Commerce (Coursework) and Masters of Translation Studies (Coursework or Coursework and Dissertation)
b92d45af-21a4-444b-88d3-8cd15d31b86e.description: This double master's degree is the only one of its kind in Australia, combining business training with professional translation studies. Students develop bilingual professional capability across English and one of eight languages, Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean or Spanish, through translation practice across a variety of text types related to diverse business contexts, alongside a full commerce specialisation. Graduates are qualified for professional employment in multilingual contexts including business, government and non-government organisations, and those who choose the coursework and dissertation pathway in Translation Studies can progress into PhD study in the field.
b92d45af-21a4-444b-88d3-8cd15d31b86e.curriculum: The combined award runs over 2.5 to 3 years full time, with part time study available, and is delivered on campus at Perth with intakes in both Semester 1 and Semester 2. The award draws its structure and unit requirements from its two component courses, the Master of Commerce (coursework) [41680] and the Master of Translation Studies (coursework or coursework and dissertation) [12520], with students completing the commerce specialisation units alongside the translation studies units, including a dissertation for those on that pathway.
b92d45af-21a4-444b-88d3-8cd15d31b86e.admission_requirements: Applicants need a bachelor's degree with a weighted average mark of at least 65 per cent in relevant Level 3 units, or at least two years of professional experience in a relevant occupation, or completion of specific UWA graduate certificates in business fields. In addition, applicants must show native or near native competency in their chosen language, or meet specific proficiency benchmarks: B2 or C1 on the Common European Framework for European languages, HSK 4 for Chinese, or JLPT N2 or N3 for Japanese, with equivalent standards applying for the other language options.
b92d45af-21a4-444b-88d3-8cd15d31b86e.english_requirements: Applicants must meet a minimum IELTS Academic score of 6.5, with no band below 6.0, corresponding to UWA's Minimum English language competence standard under the University Policy on Admission, Coursework.

3abdb9c5-2337-48bc-b6c2-718b8db71034.description: The Bachelor of Economics equips students with an understanding of how markets, businesses, governments and individuals make economic decisions, and how economic forces shape society. The course requires an ATAR of 85, with an Economics or Financial Economics major forming the core of study, and graduates go on to roles across the Reserve Bank, Treasury, financial services and consulting. The degree also provides a pathway into UWA's honours and PhD programs. Tuition is approximately A$54,500 for the full degree.
3abdb9c5-2337-48bc-b6c2-718b8db71034.curriculum: 144 credit points (24 units), 3 years full time. Structure: one mandatory major, either Economics or Financial Economics, with a maximum of 72 credit points at Level 1, a minimum of 72 credit points at Level 2 or 3, and at least 36 credit points at Level 3. The Economics major is grounded in microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics for students aiming at professional economist roles; Financial Economics focuses on how money, banking and financial markets operate. Students may add an additional major and/or up to two minors from any UWA undergraduate program within the 144 point total.
3abdb9c5-2337-48bc-b6c2-718b8db71034.admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 85, or equivalent as recognised by UWA (or an assured pathway offer / place in a relevant UWA access program). Prerequisite: a scaled ATAR score of at least 50 (or WACE grade C or better) in Mathematics Applications, with Mathematics Methods recommended; a bridging course is available for students without the required maths background.
3abdb9c5-2337-48bc-b6c2-718b8db71034.english_requirements: Standard (Minimum tier) UWA English language competence requirement: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no communicative skill below 60, or equivalent under UWA's Policy on Admission, Coursework.

63ea1e6e-d417-4b1b-bd89-97eff93ff96b.curriculum: 144 credit points (24 units), 3 years full time, with a February and July intake. This is an umbrella degree: students choose one degree specific major from Architecture A, Architecture B, Landscape Architecture, or Environmental Geography and Planning. Structure: a maximum of 72 credit points at Level 1, a minimum of 72 credit points at Level 2 or 3 (including at least 18 points at Level 3), plus foundation units as applicable. Students may add an additional major and/or up to two minors within the 144 point total. The Architecture majors introduce building and urban design through studio based learning (Architecture Studio 1 to 3) alongside history, theory, structures and construction units, and feed into UWA's postgraduate Master of Architecture.
63ea1e6e-d417-4b1b-bd89-97eff93ff96b.admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 70, or equivalent as recognised by UWA, or entry via an assured pathway offer, Experience based Entry assessment (minimum score of 100), or a relevant UWA access program. No specific ATAR subject prerequisites are required, though the Architecture majors are highly selective in practice (recent high school leaver ATAR around 90).
63ea1e6e-d417-4b1b-bd89-97eff93ff96b.english_requirements: Standard (Minimum tier) UWA English language competence requirement: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no communicative skill below 60, or equivalent under UWA's Policy on Admission, Coursework.

31cfad70-0e3b-4845-a75e-5403817d48eb.curriculum: 144 credit points (24 units), 3 years full time. One mandatory major, Hospitality Management, with a maximum of 72 credit points at Level 1 and a minimum of 72 credit points at Level 2 or 3, including at least 36 credit points at Level 3. Coursework combines core business units (accounting, economics, marketing, data analytics, business communication) with specialised hospitality management units and three structured work integrated learning internships across the degree. Students may add an optional minor within the 144 point total.
31cfad70-0e3b-4845-a75e-5403817d48eb.admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 70, or equivalent as recognised by UWA, or entry via an assured pathway offer, Experience based Entry assessment (minimum score of 100), or a relevant UWA access program. No specific ATAR subject prerequisites are required.
31cfad70-0e3b-4845-a75e-5403817d48eb.english_requirements: Standard (Minimum tier) UWA English language competence requirement: IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or PTE Academic overall score of 64 with no communicative skill below 60, or equivalent under UWA's Policy on Admission, Coursework.

b6385753-aed9-4804-bc16-de59764fce7b._name: Master of Applied Human Performance Science (coursework)
b6385753-aed9-4804-bc16-de59764fce7b.curriculum: The course covers exercise physiology, biomechanics and performance science through units including SSEH3388, SSEH3553, SSEH3554, SSEH3555, SSEH4598, SSEH5020, SSEH5021, SSEH5022, SSEH5023, SSEH5025, SSEH5026, SSEH5027, SSEH5029, SSEH5101, SSEH5102, SSEH5111, SSEH5222 and SSEH5333, spanning applied physiology, strength and conditioning, performance analysis and a research project sequence within the School of Human Sciences (Exercise and Sport Science).
